proof_summary: For \(n\ge 20\), writing \(d=s(n)\), \(e=s(d)\), and \(M=(n-e)/9\), digit-sum congruences and elementary bounds make \(M\) a positive integer and allow one to pad \(d-1\) to \(M\) digits; adjoining its digitwise 9-complement and the digits of \(d\) produces \(q=d\bigl(10^M(10^M+1)-1\bigr)\) with \(s(q)=9M+e=n\). Thus \(k=10^nq>n\) satisfies \(d\mid k\) and \(s(k)=n\mid n\), while the positive cases below 20 are checked directly.
